title: Adaptive Decision Canvas for Enterprise Data-Control Intake: scoring, routing, and enforcement for redaction/retention/PII/export requests
creator: Diego Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Enterprise customers increasingly submit ad hoc data-control requests (log redaction, retention overrides, PII handling exemptions, bulk audit exports). Current routing is inconsistent and causes slow SLAs, missed security reviews, and repeated engineering rework. Goal: create a decision canvas and scoring rubric that standardizes intake, automates routing to Legal/Security/Platform, and yields clear outcomes and owner handoffs.

Scope (non-bug): intake form fields, scoring weights, route rules, pre-approved responses for low-risk items, escalation thresholds, and the operator-runbook for manual review. Exclude: implementation changes to encryption/KMS, major infra refactors, and billing adjustments (handled separately).

Success metrics: median time to first response <= 48h for triaged items, cycle time to resolution <= 15 business days for medium risk, and % of requests auto-routed without manual touch >= 40% in first quarter post-launch.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Decision canvas documented and approved by Legal, Security, and Platform PMs.
2) Intake form implemented in Zendesk/Forms with required fields and automated tags.
3) Routing rules implemented in intake pipeline (Zendesk triggers or internal sys) and validated with 20 historical tickets.
4) Playbook for manual reviewer with checklists and canned responses published in Confluence.
5) Dashboard tracking intake counts, route outcomes, and SLA breaches is available in Looker/Metabase.
proposed_workflow: Two-stage triage: (A) Automated scoring at intake: fields map to weighted criteria (customer tier, data category, retention length, export scope, regulatory signals). Score bands: Low/Medium/High/Critical. (B) Route by band: Low -> Automated response & close (with guidance); Medium -> Platform PM + infra engineering review; High -> Security + Legal + dedicated engineering owner; Critical -> Incident-style engagement with SLA and executive notification. Include periodic re-eval step after 7 days for Medium/High to ensure no emergent risk.
routing_matrix_summary:
Key signals and routing examples: 
- Retention override <=30 days & non-PII -> Low (auto-approve)
- Retention 31-365 days & pseudonymous data -> Medium (platform review)
- Request to remove PII from logs (names, emails) with customer legal order -> High (legal + security)
- Bulk audit export for >100k user records or cross-border -> Critical (exec notif + security review)
Weighting example: customer_tier (40%), data_sensitivity (30%), scope_size (20%), regulatory_flag (10%).
triage_rubric:
Fields and scoring: 
- Customer tier: tier-enterprise=3, tier-midmarket=2, tier-self-serve=1
- Data classification: highly_sensitive=5, sensitive=3, pseudonymous=2, non_personal=0
- Retention length requested: >365 days=4, 90-365=3, 31-89=2, <=30=0
- Export scope: >100k records=4, 10k-100k=3, <10k=1
- Legal/regulatory flag: yes=5, no=0
- Requested action type: full-redaction=4, redact-fields=3, retention-change=2, export=3
Aggregate score -> bands: 0-5 Low, 6-11 Medium, 12-16 High, 17+ Critical.
Include explicit override rules: Security or Legal can escalate any Medium->High with justification. Engineering can request reclassification to Medium with documented mitigation (e.g., sampled redaction pipeline).
owner_notes: Proposed pilot: run decision canvas retroactively on 60 closed support tickets (security & PM to validate). If pilot yields >=40% auto-route rate for low items and SLA improvements, phase roll-out: 1) intake form + tagging, 2) automated routing, 3) canned responses and runbook, 4) dashboard and monthly review. Coordinate with Platform SRE for backstop controls (rate-limits on export jobs).
